study_identification_part.si_4_title: Dynamic gray matter volume changes in pediatric multiple sclerosis: A 3.5 year MRI study

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used linear mixed-effects models (LMM) to estimate normative sex- and age-expected GM growth curves. The model was fitted voxel-wise to healthy control preprocessed GM maps using Matlab's 'fitlme' function (Statistics and Machine Learning Toolbox). The model included fixed effects for age (linear and quadratic terms), sex, age-sex interaction, and magnetic field strength, plus random effects for subject (random intercept and slope for age).
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: To estimate normative sex- and age-expected GM growth curves, using Matlab's 'fitlme' function (Statistics and Machine Learning Toolbox), the following linear mixed-effects model was fitted voxel-wise to HC preprocessed GM maps

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Gray matter (GM) volume at the voxel level was the response variable. Preprocessed GM maps were modulated, smoothed with a 4-mm Gaussian kernel, and normalized to MNI space using DARTEL. The outcome variable Yij represents the GM amount at voxel level for participant i at time point j.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: where Yij represents the GM amount at voxel level

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The model included: (1) mean-centered age as a linear term, (2) age-squared (quadratic term), (3) sex as a binary variable, (4) age-by-sex interaction, (5) magnetic field strength (MFS) as a binary variable to account for differences between 1.5T (NIH HC) and 3.0T (HSR) scanners, and (6) subject-level random effects with bivariate normal distribution for random intercept and slope.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: where Yij represents the GM amount at voxel level, Ageij the mean-centered age, Sexi the sex (binary variable) of participant i at time point j. Another binary variable to account for differences in magnetic field strength (MFSi) and acquisition protocol was also added to overcome potential biases. A bivariate normal distribution was assumed for the vector of random effects (bi0, bi1), independent of the homoscedastic normal error term.
